neighbours.label: A small number word that counts enemy military hardware being destroyed, lost or captured (sinking four enemy destroyers)
fire: The submarine managed to sink three enemy freighters in one week.
Our gunners destroyed five enemy bombers before they reached the coast.
The patrol captured two enemy trucks on the mountain road.
By evening the squadron had shot down six enemy fighters.
The raid knocked out four enemy radar stations along the shore.
The division lost seven armored cars and three field guns that day.
Partisans blew up two enemy supply trains outside the city.
The cruiser sank three enemy gunboats in the strait.
quiet: The submarine managed to sink the enemy freighter in one week.
Our gunners destroyed the enemy bombers before they reached the coast.
The patrol captured an enemy truck on the mountain road.
By evening the squadron had shot down the enemy fighters.
The baker sold four cherry pies along the shore that morning.
The family lost seven old photos and three letters that day.
Students handed in two long essays outside the office.
The cook made three big pots of soup in the kitchen.

notes: Card: ' four' Japanese aircraft carriers, ' five' companies, 'total number of earthquakes', digits in a code constant. Probes: sinking four enemy destroyers 0.76, captured four government tanks 0.37, destroy three enemy bridges 0.36, lost two aircraft carriers 0.30; four apples 0.02, five companies of infantry 0.05, total number of hurricanes 0.14, the same battle sentence without a number 0.01. The + pole counts people (membership, employs 30, seats 19), so this pole may be the counts-of-things side; only the military case is tested here.
